speaker: The Court Painter
message: Sire, the great hall lacks a portrait worthy of your reign. I would need gold leaf. Quite a lot of gold leaf.

speaker: The Sculptor
message: A statue of Your Majesty, forty feet high, at the harbour mouth. Ships would steer by your face.

speaker: The Herald
message: The neighbouring queen's poets call her 'the Magnificent'. Your poets call you 'the Adequate'. I could have them flogged.

speaker: The Tailor
message: The new robes need ermine from the north, which is at war, and silk from the south, which is at plague. But Majesty, the drape.

speaker: The Master of Ceremonies
message: A festival in your honour. Three days. The people would need the days off, and the bread would need to be free.

speaker: The Chronicler
message: I am writing the history of your reign. Would Your Majesty prefer that I record the lost battle at the ford, or that the ford never existed?

speaker: The Duke
message: At the tourney, the champion has offered to lose to you. Publicly. He asks only a small estate for the trouble.

speaker: The Ambassador
message: The Emperor invites you to his court. You would be seated below his nephews. His nephews are eleven.

speaker: The Mint Master
message: Your face on the coin has been called 'jowly'. A new die is costly, but the chin could be improved.

speaker: A Child
message: My mother says the king is very handsome and also that the roof leaks.

speaker: The Playwright
message: My new play has a wise king in it. The wise king is you, Sire, though the wise king dies in act four. It is a tragedy.

speaker: The Bishop
message: A stained glass window showing Your Majesty among the saints. The theologians object, but theologians object to everything.

speaker: The General
message: The mountain pass is impregnable. But they have called you a coward for not taking it.

speaker: The Poet Laureate
message: I have composed an epic of your deeds. It runs to forty thousand lines. The reading will take four days, and the court must attend.

speaker: The Bishop
message: Your Majesty, a saint's finger bone has been found in the mud outside the abbey. A cathedral would be fitting. A very large cathedral.
right: A finger is not a saint

speaker: The Abbot
message: The monastery would like the forest. The forest currently feeds the villages, but the villages could learn to fast.

speaker: The Confessor
message: Your Majesty's sins are many. A pilgrimage would help. The realm can be governed by letter for a year.

speaker: The Inquisitor
message: There are heretics in the eastern town. Also tax collectors, but mostly heretics.

speaker: A Prophet
message: The stars say a great ruler will be undone by their own hand this year. But not you, Majesty. Obviously not you. Unless you doubt the stars.

speaker: The Archbishop
message: The church's tithe is a tenth. Scripture says nothing about it staying a tenth.

speaker: The Physician
message: The plague spreads. The bishop says prayer will end it. I say quarantine will end it. The bishop outranks me.

speaker: The Treasurer
message: The church asks to be exempt from all taxes. In perpetuity. Backdated.

speaker: The Sister of Charity
message: The orphans need a house. The church will build it if the crown pays for it and the church owns it.

speaker: The Bishop
message: A comet. The clergy say it foretells doom unless the army is disbanded, as a gesture of faith.
right: It is a rock in the sky

speaker: The Cardinal
message: The Pope's envoy requires the crown to kneel. In public. On the cobbles.

speaker: The Village Elder
message: The new church would sit exactly where the well is. The priest says God will provide water.

speaker: The Zealot
message: A holy war, Sire. The infidels are far away and well armed, but the cause is righteous.

speaker: The Bishop
message: The monks have found that Your Majesty's grandfather was born out of wedlock. The record can be corrected, for a donation.

speaker: The Treasurer
message: Sire, the vault holds less than it did. The merchants offer a loan at a rate I would call generous, if I were the one being paid.

speaker: The Merchant
message: A monopoly on salt, Sire, in exchange for half the profits. The price of salt would, regrettably, triple. Salt is how the poor keep meat through winter.

speaker: The Alchemist
message: I have turned lead into gold. Once. In private. I need only a thousand crowns to do it again.

speaker: The Tax Collector
message: The peasants hide grain. If we tax the grain they have not grown yet, they cannot hide it.

speaker: The Foreign Banker
message: We would like to buy the harbour. Outright. The gold would fill the treasury twice over. The fishermen, the customs men, and the navy would need somewhere else to be.

speaker: The Spymaster
message: The Duke has hidden wealth. If he were found guilty of something, the wealth would be yours. The other dukes would notice. The Duke's regiments would notice first.

speaker: The Mine Foreman
message: The silver seam runs under the cathedral. Digging would be very profitable and very loud.

speaker: The Widow
message: My husband's land was seized for a debt he did not owe. I ask for it back. It is good land, and the whole village is watching to see what the crown does with it.

speaker: The Shipwright
message: A fleet of trade ships. The army's budget would cover it, if the army did not mind.

speaker: The Minister of Roads
message: Tolls on every road. Every bridge. Every ford. The people would grumble, but they would pay.

speaker: The Envoy
message: The neighbouring king offers a fortune for the border province. The people there are fond of you, apparently. The garrison there is fond of the people, and the bishop has a cathedral in it.

speaker: The Physician
message: The plague spreads in the poor quarter. Treating it costs gold. Walling it off costs bricks.

speaker: The Guildmaster
message: The guild will pay handsomely for a law banning foreign cloth. The foreign cloth is cheaper and better, and it is what the people and the soldiers actually wear.

speaker: The Steward
message: The royal granary could be sold now at a fine price. Winter is, admittedly, coming.

speaker: The General
message: The border lord to the east has stopped sending tribute. He says his roads flooded. His roads did not flood.

speaker: The General
message: The neighbouring kingdom's harvest failed. They are weak. They are also our closest ally.

speaker: The Marshal
message: The bandits in the hills number about twelve. I propose four thousand men.

speaker: The Ambassador
message: An insult from the Emperor's court. Something about your horse. War would be justified, technically.

speaker: The Armourer
message: New cannon. They would cost the treasury half of everything, and we are at peace with everyone.

speaker: The Admiral
message: Pirates in the strait. Burning their port would end them, though the port is technically the Emperor's.

speaker: A Peasant
message: The soldiers are eating our sheep, Sire. They say it is training.

speaker: The General
message: The peasants riot over bread. I could restore order by nightfall. Some of the peasants would not see nightfall.

speaker: The Spymaster
message: The Duke has raised his own guard. It is probably for his own protection. Probably.

speaker: The Recruiting Sergeant
message: Conscription. Every third son. The fields would suffer but the ranks would swell.

speaker: The Bishop
message: The church asks the army to guard the pilgrim road. It would pull soldiers from the border.

speaker: The Scout
message: There is a mountain kingdom no one has conquered. There is a reason no one has conquered it.

speaker: The Envoy
message: A peace treaty. Both sides reduce their armies by half. They will honour it, probably.

speaker: The Old Knight
message: Tournament season. The knights want a real war instead; the practice is dull.

speaker: The Spymaster
message: I have a list of names. Some are certainly traitors. Some are certainly not. I cannot yet tell you which is which.

speaker: The Cook
message: Someone has been in the kitchens at night, Sire. It was probably a cat. Probably.

speaker: The Chancellor
message: Your brother has been very generous to the army lately. Very generous. He says it is patriotism.

speaker: The Bishop
message: The clergy prayed for Your Majesty's health this morning. They did not pray for it last week.

speaker: The Physician
message: Your tonic. It is the same tonic as always. I brewed it myself. As always.

speaker: The Captain of the Guard
message: Double the guard, triple the locks, move your bedchamber nightly. Nobody would know where you sleep. Including me.

speaker: The Ambassador
message: A gift from the neighbouring queen: a very fine horse. It has not been checked for anything.

speaker: The Spymaster
message: I have found no plots this month. Which is exactly what a plotter would want me to find.

speaker: The Peasant Delegation
message: The villages ask for a meeting with the crown. All of the villages. At once.

speaker: The Treasurer
message: The accounts balance perfectly, Sire. To the penny. For the first time ever.

speaker: The General
message: The army loves you, Sire. They chant your name. They also chant mine, but quieter.

speaker: The Astrologer
message: A traitor sits at your table. The stars are unclear on which chair.

speaker: The Spymaster
message: I could read every letter in the realm. It would take a thousand clerks, and the people would find out.

speaker: The Chancellor
message: A new law: any who speak ill of the crown lose their tongue. Fewer people would speak ill of the crown.

speaker: A Peasant
message: Begging your pardon, Majesty, but the mill wheel broke and the miller says fixing it is the crown's job, and the crown says it is the miller's job, and meanwhile there is no bread.

speaker: The Chancellor
message: There are forty petitions waiting. I could read them to you, or I could tell you they are all fine.

speaker: The Steward
message: The dam upstream has a crack. It could be fixed now, cheaply, or later, expensively, or never, dramatically.

speaker: The General
message: The border garrison asks for relief. They have been there four years. The replacement would need organising.

speaker: The Treasurer
message: I could manage the treasury entirely without Your Majesty's signature. It would save you so much reading.

speaker: The Physician
message: You have not moved from that chair in three days. Medically, I must object. Personally, I understand.

speaker: The Ambassador
message: The Emperor's envoy has waited a week. He is starting to take it personally.

speaker: The Bishop
message: The feast of the patron saint requires the crown to walk to the cathedral. It is a long walk.

speaker: The Cook
message: The kitchens request a decision on the winter menu. It is a large document.

speaker: The Chancellor
message: The old laws contradict the new laws. Someone should sort them out. It would take years.

speaker: The Duke
message: The council proposes governing in your name while you rest. It would be a great weight off your shoulders.

speaker: A Peasant
message: The bridge fell in. The other bridge is only four hours away. We can manage.

speaker: The Spymaster
message: A rumour of treason. Investigating would mean interviews. Many interviews.

speaker: The Master of Horse
message: The royal hunt is tomorrow. Or it could be next month. Or never.

speaker: The Ambassador
message: Our neighbour proposes a marriage between your heir and theirs. They ask only a modest dowry, three provinces, and the right to garrison your northern forts.

speaker: The Village Elder
message: The river changed course. Half the farms are now in the neighbouring kingdom. The farmers ask what they are.

speaker: The Physician
message: A plague ship in the harbour. The sailors beg to land.

speaker: The Treasurer
message: The harvest was good. There is a surplus. For once.

speaker: The Bishop
message: A miracle in the north: a statue wept. Pilgrims are coming. Many pilgrims, few inns.

speaker: The General
message: A neighbouring prince asks for refuge. His brother wants him dead. His brother has an army.

speaker: The Stonemason
message: The castle wall is sound. The tower is not. I mention this because you are standing in it.

speaker: The Merchant
message: Traders from a far land bring a strange leaf that is brewed in water. They say it will change everything.

speaker: The Scholar
message: I have built a machine that prints books. The church would like it burned. The merchants would like six.

speaker: The Judge
message: A nobleman killed a peasant in a brawl. The law says hang him. The nobles say otherwise.

speaker: The Farmer
message: The lord takes half our harvest. The law says a third. The lord says the law is old.

speaker: The Envoy
message: The Emperor requests tribute. A modest sum. He also requested it from the last king, who refused, briefly.
